Hi all — attaching the diagram and control matrix draft. High-level notes below; see attachments for the visual and the SIG/CAIQ mapping.

Attachment stubs: redwood_airbridge_topology_v1.pdf (diagram), airbridge_control_matrix.xlsx (control mapping)

Executive summary (short):
- Purpose: demonstrate logical and operational separation between Redwood Dedicated GPU pools (multi-tenant, reserved) and Private deployments (customer VPCs or on-prem agents). We use an "airbridge" concept to describe the minimal, policy-governed interconnect points used only for management/control plane telemetry and signed artifacts replication.

Key controls called out on the diagram:
- Control-plane segregation: Dedicated control plane runs in Redwood-managed tenancy; Private control plane endpoints are customer-managed (VPC endpoints or on-prem control plane components). No shared plaintext metadata paths; all control-plane APIs enforce mutual TLS + client cert pinning.
- KMS/HSM boundaries: Customer-managed keys are stored in customer KMS/HSM for Private installs; hosted/Dedicated tenants may use Redwood-managed KMS with envelope encryption. Diagram annotates which keys are allowed to leave the customer boundary (none).
- Egress & egress-proofing: Service-edge proxies enforce allowlists per tenant and implement TLS interception only for telemetry (hashed, non-PHI). Egress gateway ACLs are configurable per-customer for Private via an agent.
- Sidecar placement: For Private, inference runtime sidecars run inside customer VPCs with explicit subnet scoping; these sidecars handle local KV cache and tokenization — no shard-level secrets are sent to Redwood without explicit opt-in.
- Audit & logging: Control plane emits token-level traces to a locked audit cluster with retention configurable per-customer. Logs for Private installs can be pushed to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets (push model), preventing sign-in level logs leaving customer storage.

Fallback & residency:
- Model fallback is region-aware. If a primary (hosted/dedicated) model variant is unavailable, the router will attempt same-region compatible variants (pinned to the same region) before attempting cross-region variants. Cross-region fallbacks are disabled by default for Private installs unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region failover in their VPC configuration. We documented this behavior in the diagram callout.

Open items for Sam:
1) Confirm whether BlueRiver requires cross-region failover to be disallowed in our Hosted/Dedicated offering as well (we default to allow within jurisdictional bounds).
2) Any preferred SIG/CAIQ control IDs you'd like prioritized (we mapped the common network/KMS/logging IDs in the spreadsheet).

Thanks — we can iterate quickly on the diagram.
